correctness.rationale: Since E^2 has unique nonzero u, each natural-basis square is u by nondegeneracy; natural bases exactly B-orthonormal frames. The characteristic vector c=sum e_i in every orthonormal frame; graph outdegree is the coordinate weight k of u, which has norm parity s and k=n iff u=c. Coordinate permutations and weight-four isotropic transvections T_w(x)=x+B(x,w)w change weight by +/-2 and connect all permitted noncharacteristic vectors of equal norm parity, proving exact orbit and binomial frequencies. Independently enumerated every ordered orthonormal frame over F2 in n=1..5 (counts 1,2,6,48,720) and checked all nonzero u and every predicted support probability.

evidence: The 2025 classification of commutative algebras with one-dimensional square identifies their bilinear-form structure but does not specify every natural-basis digraph or its exact distribution. Kramer–Stroppel work on the same bilinear isometry groups and likely implies some orbit facts, but focuses on Hodge/exterior-power actions rather than evolution-algebra graph spectra. Recent evolution-algebra surveys ask for such natural-basis graph invariants. Classical orbit theory may make the graph law a short corollary, and that priority risk is recorded.

final_claim: For nondegenerate evolution algebras over F2 with dim E^2=1, B defined by xy=B(x,y)u is nonsingular symmetric and natural bases are orthonormal bases. With B-characteristic vector c, if u=c all natural-basis graphs are G_(n,n); otherwise the graph support sizes are exactly 1<=k<n with k parity B(u,u), and conditional law over uniform ordered natural bases is binom(n,k)/(2^(n-1)-1_(s=0)-1_(s=n mod 2)).
